report.summary: Reviewed chunk 1 of daedalus/council/vendors.py (header, constants, identity helpers, VendorReply, FloorRefusal). Claims mostly kept or uncheckable; no defects found.

handoff.purpose: Module header, closed vocabularies, host constants, identity helpers, VendorReply and FloorRefusal dataclasses.

symbols.name: STATUSES
symbols.note: Closed tuple of five transport statuses: ok, unavailable, timeout, refused_by_floor, error.

symbols.name: LANES
symbols.note: Tuple of two egress lanes: trusted and untrusted.

symbols.name: UNAVAILABLE_REASONS
symbols.note: Closed tuple of ten machine reasons for unavailability.

symbols.name: PROMPT_DATA_NOTICE
symbols.note: Prompt injection notice prepended to every outbound prompt.

symbols.name: _slug
symbols.note: Normalises a model id into a safe actor segment using regex substitution.

symbols.name: actor_id
symbols.note: Builds council.<vendor>.<model> actor id via bus.actor_id after slugifying vendor and model.

symbols.name: model_family
symbols.note: Coarse weight family from a model string, stripping tag and trailing size/version tokens.

symbols.name: VendorReply
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass holding one vendor's reply: transport status, content, provenance, independence class, lane, withheld paths.

symbols.name: FloorRefusal
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass naming a secret-floor rule and channel.

claims.text: This module produces EVIDENCE, never a decision. :class:`VendorReply` carries no approve/reject/score/verdict/majority field and must never grow one
claims.why: VendorReply fields are vendor, actor, model, status, content, latency_s, reason, stderr, usage, independence_class, endpoint, cli_version, lane, local, withheld. None is approve/reject/score/verdict/majority.

claims.text: ``status`` here is a TRANSPORT status (did the bytes make the round trip), not a judgement about the work under review.
claims.why: STATUSES contains only ok, unavailable, timeout, refused_by_floor, error; no judgement values.

claims.text: CLOSED -- an adapter may not invent a sixth.
claims.why: STATUSES is a fixed tuple of five strings; __post_init__ validates status against it, so any other value raises ValueError.

claims.text: ``untrusted`` turns the allow-list / default-deny tier ON (``sensitivity.slice_egress_rule``).
claims.why: The actual invocation of slice_egress_rule is not in this chunk; only the lane constant is defined.

claims.text: Machine reasons -- never free prose -- so a council record can be aggregated.
claims.why: UNAVAILABLE_REASONS is a fixed tuple of ten machine-readable strings; no free prose is present.

claims.text: Not "localhost": avoids the IPv6 (::1) miss on Windows, same as providers/ollama.py.
claims.why: The IPv6 claim references providers/ollama.py, which is not in this chunk.
The constant is defined but its use in outbound prompts is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: Make a model id safe for an actor segment without losing information.
claims.why: Regex replaces runs of characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] with a single hyphen; empty result becomes 'unknown'.
The format is delegated to bus.actor_id; the actual format string is not in this chunk.

claims.text: The FORMAT is delegated to :func:`bus.actor_id` so the id on a transcript turn and the id on the reply that produced it cannot drift apart; this function only normalises the raw model id first (a raw ``qwen2.5-coder:7b`` would otherwise put a colon in a durable identifier).
claims.why: actor_id calls _bus_actor_id(_slug(vendor), _slug(model)) after slugifying, which replaces colons with hyphens.

claims.text: The unit of independence is WEIGHTS, not endpoints. Local ``qwen2.5-coder:7b`` and bench ``qwen2.5-coder:7b`` are one voice on two sockets
claims.why: model_family strips vendor/host prefixes and tags, producing the same family for identical model names regardless of endpoint.

claims.text: Heuristic and deliberately coarse -- it strips the tag (``:7b``) and any trailing size/version token, so it OVER-merges rather than under-merges.
claims.why: The code splits on ':' and takes the first part, then repeatedly pops trailing tokens matching size/version patterns like 7b, v2, latest, 20240101.

claims.text: Deliberately carries NO approve/reject/pass/verdict/ok/score/confidence field, and must never grow one
claims.why: VendorReply fields are vendor, actor, model, status, content, latency_s, reason, stderr, usage, independence_class, endpoint, cli_version, lane, local, withheld. None of the forbidden fields is present.

claims.text: ``status`` is transport, ``content`` is prose for a human and for a claim extractor, and everything else is provenance so the turn can be re-run and compared.
claims.why: The fields match this description: status is one of STATUSES, content is a string, and the remaining fields are provenance metadata.

claims.text: Machine reason from :data:`UNAVAILABLE_REASONS`, or a secret-floor rule LABEL (never the matched bytes). Empty when ``status == "ok"``.
claims.why: The reason field exists with that comment, but enforcement of 'empty when ok' and the secret-floor label rule is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Evidence paths withheld by the tier-2 allow-list on an untrusted lane.
claims.why: The field exists, but the actual withholding logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: A secret-floor hit. Names the RULE, never the matched bytes.
claims.why: FloorRefusal has only rule and channel fields; no bytes field is present.
The comment is present, but enforcement that channel is limited to those three values is not in this chunk.

observations.what: VendorReply.__post_init__ validates status and lane against closed sets, enforcing the closed vocabulary.
